summary:
THE HIGH REFUTATION REPRODUCES EXACTLY, THEN IS REPAIRED AND THE REPAIR IS PROVED. I planted the historical defect -- a hardcoded FAB_<LEVER>=<literal> in the reason -- on each of the nine gates in EQUATION_GATES, one mirror per gate, one find/replace each, and on the file as it stood a bare `0` was UNDETECTED on exactly the five they named (fab.balance, fab.explore, fab.discover, fab.breadth_cap, fab.identity_round_trip: exit 0, '=== 8 checks, 0 failing ==='), caught on the other four; a `0.0` was UNDETECTED on ALL NINE. The other direction reproduces too: a CORRECT reason reformatted `f"FAB_EC_W={ec_w:g}"` FAILED F7 (exit 1), and a hardcoded gate VALUE with a correct reason (value="ec_w=0.0") PASSED. Undersensitive to the defect, oversensitive to a reformat. THE REPAIR IS A WIDER DOMAIN, NOT A TIGHTER STRING: fabric/api.py::build refuses `v < 0.0` and -0.0 is not less than 0.0, so a twelfth arm assembles all nine levers at NEGATIVE ZERO -- I verified the frozen Config really reads -0.0 on all nine fields and all nine reasons really print '-0.0' -- which makes the reachable domain of those nine `<= 0.0` branches EXACTLY {+0.0, -0.0}, both swept, so any constant is wrong on one of the two. The comparison keeps the sign (math.copysign) and the arithmetic cross-check is kept but made NUMERIC instead of textual. RESULT, 27 plants: 27 caught (nine gates x `0`, `0.0`, `-0.0`), 0 undetected; both reformat controls pass; the hardcoded-VALUE class, which the old check missed, is now caught. The check no longer overstates: dropping either zero arm makes F7 FAIL on its own coverage census rather than pass, and the detail line NAMES the eight (gate,lever) pairs it cannot catch (fab.halt/FAB_HALT, fab.route_learned/FAB_ROUTE_LEARN and six more, whose reasons are emitted only when the lever is off, so they are read at one value and a constant there is invisible). The docstring was rewritten to say all of this. THE TRAP WAS NOT TAKEN: EQUATION_GATES still holds all nine.

SIX MORE REPAIRS, EACH RE-PROVED BY REVERTING IT IN A SCRATCH COPY OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY. F2 ran two cache states over three rows (I traced it: both step-5 rows enter the same-window branch, which returns before any write site) and never entered the MIDDLE branch, the only one holding `pop.ident_graph = None`; it now runs three rows at FAB_EMB_EVERY 1/1/4, identifies which branch ran from the OBJECT RETURNED rather than by re-deriving the predicate, and asserts that three distinct branches were entered. Load-bearing: leaving ONLY the middle write site unguarded is exit 0 on the old file and exit 1 now; collapsing the rows back to two states FAILS on the branch census. F8 held D4's switch to NOTHING (flipping REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD to False, or replacing FAB's guard with `if False:`, each left the old file at exit 0) because assemble.build raises first; it now pushes the negative at TWO doors, the second being `assemble.build(..., couplings=[])`, which src/fabric/api.py::manage_period's own comment names as the way to reach FAB's guard -- both S1 and S2 are exit 0 old, exit 1 now. F8's 'names the lever' assertion was satisfied by a historical anecdote in spine/derive.py about a DIFFERENT value; it now (a) makes the VALUE move (two negatives, each message must carry its own standalone number and not the other's) and (b) tests the lever by DIRECTED ADJACENCY to the value read, reporting per layer who does and who does not -- rewording that anecdote was exit 1 on the old file and is exit 0 now, which is the false coupling gone. F4's 'names the lever' half could not fail for the three REVERSED levers (static prose names all three whichever was refused): stripping the names out of build's generated list reported 8 of 11 rows before and reports 11 of 11 now. F1's twelve n>=2 cells asserted finiteness only: one analytic n=2 cell now separates the unbiased estimator from the biased one and from a deleted term -- zeroing the n>=2 variance term and switching it to biased were both exit 0 before and are both exit 1 now, each named in the finding. AND THE RUNNER: `_report`'s `vacuous` argument only appended a string, so a check that examined nothing printed 'PASS ... (VACUOUS: 0 examined)' and exited 0 -- a sentence contradicting itself in the one file whose purpose is assurance; it now FAILS (proved both ways on a forced-vacuous mirror).

findings.detail:
THE REFUTATION IS CORRECT AND I REPRODUCED IT BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING, all nine gates, one plant at a time, one find/replace each into the reason's f-string. At the bare `0` spelling five of nine went UNDETECTED -- fab.balance, fab.explore, fab.discover, fab.breadth_cap, fab.identity_round_trip, each exit 0 with '=== 8 checks, 0 failing ===' -- and only fab.expert_choice, fab.distinctness, fab.hop_sup and fab.independence were caught. At the `0.0` spelling NINE of nine went undetected. The cause is exactly as filed: the check searched for the printed token as TEXT inside `f"{gate.value} {gate.threshold}"`, the whole concatenation, which carries unrelated numbers ('0 row(s) swapped', 'limit=0 of', the literal threshold '> 0', '0 embedding(s) scored'). And the oversensitivity reproduces too: a CORRECT reason reformatted to `f"FAB_EC_W={ec_w:g}"` made F7 FAIL, while a hardcoded gate VALUE (value="ec_w=0.0") with a correct reason PASSED -- the mirror image of the defect, invisible.

THE REPAIR. F4 refuses `v < 0.0` and -0.0 is not less than 0.0, so I added a twelfth arm at FAB_<lever>=-0.0 for all nine, and the check now VERIFIES per field that the frozen Config really holds -0.0 before drawing any conclusion from that arm (if a parser ever flattened the sign the arm would silently stop discriminating, so that is a finding of its own). Comparison is by `_reads_the_same`, numeric with math.copysign so +0.0 and -0.0 are two readings. The arithmetic cross-check is KEPT -- it is the only thing holding the gate's own value/threshold to the same standard -- but rewritten to compare NUMBERS parsed out of the arithmetic rather than to search for a text token, which removes the reformat false-positive while keeping the hardcoded-VALUE catch. The reachable domain of all nine branches is now provably exactly two values, +0.0 and -0.0, both swept, so ANY constant is wrong on at least one arm.

WHAT IT NOW CATCHES: 27 of 27 plants (nine gates x `0`, `0.0`, `-0.0`). WHAT IT DOES NOT, printed in the check's own detail line every run rather than left to a docstring: the other 8 (gate,lever) pairs the sweep covers -- fab.forward.routed/FAB_NORM_ONLY, fab.forward.routed/FAB_ON, fab.halt/FAB_HALT, fab.halt_spent_on_base/FAB_SOCIETY, fab.identity_round_trip/FAB_SPAWN, fab.independence/FAB_SOCIETY, fab.route_learned/FAB_ROUTE_LEARN, fab.spawn/FAB_SPAWN -- are read at ONE value on every arm, because those reasons are emitted only when the lever is off, so a constant equal to that one reading is invisible and is NOT claimed to be caught. The docstring was rewritten to state exactly this and no longer says 'a literal typed into either of them does not [pass]' without qualification. EQUATION_GATES still holds all nine: the trap was not taken, and dropping an arm now FAILS on the coverage census instead of going green.

I reproduced it: `REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD = True` flipped to False left the file at exit 0 / 8 checks 0 failing, and replacing FAB's whole guard with `if False:` also left it at exit 0 -- because spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows raises inside the FAB.d_manage_period coupling during assemble.build, so the entire `else` limb that reads the switch is dead. THE FIX IS A SECOND DOOR, NOT A WEAKER ASSERTION: `assemble.build(environ, couplings=[])` is a parameter of spine/assemble.py::build and is the call src/fabric/api.py::manage_period's own comment names as the only way left to hand FAB's guard a frozen Config carrying a negative. I verified it works on this tree (build succeeds with no warnings, FAB.manage_period raises LeverError naming 'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-5'). Both doors are now pushed, so both positions of D4's switch bind. (b) THE NAMING ASSERTION PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON. I located it myself: the assembly's 992-character UnitError carries '-5' at offset 45 (a reading, in 'period_windows=Windows(-5)') and 'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY' at offset 294, inside a historical example about a DIFFERENT value ('FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 built FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1)'). REPAIRED TWO WAYS: the VALUE half is now causal (two negatives, -5 and -7, are pushed, and each refusal's message must carry its own value as a standalone number and must NOT carry the other's -- which a paragraph about -500 cannot satisfy), and the LEVER half is tested by DIRECTED ADJACENCY (the name must appear BEFORE the value it read, within a few characters, so 'FAB_X=-0.5' / 'FAB_X: -0.5' / 'FAB_X is -0.5' all pass and a name 249 characters away beside a different number does not). What is ASSERTED is that SOME layer on the path names both; what is REPORTED, per layer, every run, is which does and which does not -- today FAB.manage_period does and spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows does not, because a generic conversion is not handed the name of the lever whose wire it is computing. findings.detail: The verdict on F1's n=1 repair stands (CONFIRMED_CORRECT) and I did not re-litigate it. The coverage gap the checker filed in unfinished rather than as a finding is real and I closed it: the twelve n>=2 shape cells asserted FINITENESS ONLY, and 0.0 is finite, and so is a biased estimator. I reproduced both consequences -- multiplying `_var_cov`'s n>=2 variance term by 0.0, i.e. deleting the anti-collapse pressure the function exists for against a measured nearest-neighbour distance of 0.000, left the suite at exit 0 / 8 checks 0 failing; switching `z.var(0)` to `z.var(0, unbiased=False)`, which the n<2 branch's own comment says must stay distinguishable, also left it at exit 0. ADDED one analytic n=2 cell, chosen so it separates all three readings: at z=[[0.5],[-0.5]] the rows are already centred, so the unbiased variance is 2a^2=0.5 and the biased one is a^2=0.25, and the hinge gives 1-sqrt(0.5001)=0.2928225116705142 against 1-sqrt(0.2501)=0.4999 -- a gap of 0.207 -- while a deleted term reads 0.0. The shipped function returns 0.2928224802017212, which agrees with the analytic value to 3.1e-8. a=0.5 rather than a=1.0 because at a=1.0 the hinge floors at 0.0 under BOTH estimators and the cell would be green over the difference it exists to see.
